description: PHASE A — Verify and make OBSERVABLE the live Anthropic Claude crisis-response path, and stop the daily budget cap from silently starving real users onto the clinical fallback. The site already uses live Claude (core/comprehension_engine.py respond(), model from env INNERLIGHT_MODEL default 'claude-sonnet-4-6', key from env ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) as the PRIMARY path in /api/checkin (~line 10816-10920) and /api/innerlight/learn follow-up (~line 11199-11225). The clinical/repetitive lines the founder disliked come from the LOCAL FALLBACK (core/crisis_response_core.py public_response, core/conversation_engine.py, core/innerlight_learning_module.py _response_for_state) used only when smart==None (no key / API failure / _over_the_line twice) OR when the daily budget cap is hit. ROOT-CAUSE FINDING: _budget_ok('claude') is called at the very top of /api/checkin and INCREMENTS the counter on EVERY check-in message — even messages where Claude is not actually the decider — and when count>=CAP_CLAUDE_PER_DAY (default 1500) the whole route returns _gentle_429() a 'busy' message, not the fallback. So the cap both (a) drains far faster than real Claude usage and (b) hard-fails the route rather than degrading. Make the live-vs-fallback decision observable, log every fallback reason (NEVER the key), count the cap against ACTUAL Claude calls, warn near the cap, and make the cap configurable/safer. HYBRID IS PRESERVED: live AI stays primary, local lines remain only as fallback (Principle 15 architecture: model name in config, honest on failure).
steps: Add a daily AI-source telemetry counter near the budget block (~line 11569 in core/axiom_harmony_unified_app.py): a thread-safe _AI_SOURCE dict keyed by day with counts for {live, fallback_no_key, fallback_api_error, fallback_over_line, fallback_budget, fallback_noneng} plus last_fallback_reason and last_fallback_at. Add a helper _mark_ai_source(kind, reason='') that rolls over daily and increments. NEVER store or log the API key or any request/response content — counts and a short reason string only.

Make comprehension_engine.respond() report WHY it returned None so the caller can classify the fallback. Minimal-risk approach: add an optional out-param or a lightweight module-level last-reason accessor (e.g. comprehension_engine.last_fallback_reason() returning one of 'no_key'|'empty'|'api_error'|'over_line'|'') set inside respond()'s branches (key missing, empty text, exception, _over_the_line-twice). Do NOT change respond()'s existing return contract (dict or None) that callers depend on. Do NOT print the key; the existing print in respond() already prints only str(e)[:120] — keep that.

In /api/checkin (~10816) and /api/innerlight/learn (~11199): after the smart = comprehension_engine.respond(...) call, record telemetry — if smart: _mark_ai_source('live'); else classify via comprehension_engine.last_fallback_reason() into fallback_no_key/api_error/over_line, or 'fallback_noneng' when the non-English honest line is used. Ensure EVERY fallback logs a one-line reason via print (no key, no content) so there are no silent failures.

FIX THE BUDGET CAP SEMANTICS so it no longer starves real users: move/gate the _budget_ok('claude') accounting so the daily counter is charged for ACTUAL Claude API calls (a real respond() attempt with a key present), not for every /api/checkin hit regardless. Concretely: at route entry keep the per-IP _rate_ok('checkin',...) abuse limit, but only consume claude budget around the real model call (e.g. check budget and increment immediately before comprehension_engine.respond when a key is configured; when no key is set, do not consume claude budget at all since no spend occurs). When the cap IS reached, DO NOT hard-429 the crisis route — instead allow the request to proceed and fall through to the local warm fallback (Principle 1 no-dead-end: a person in crisis is never turned away with 'busy'), and mark _mark_ai_source('fallback_budget'). Keep _rate_ok abuse protection intact for cost-collapse defense. Preserve _gentle_429 for the genuinely abusive per-IP rate case only.

Make the cap configurable and safer: keep CAP_CLAUDE_PER_DAY env (default 1500) but add a soft-warn threshold (e.g. env CAP_CLAUDE_WARN_AT default 80 percent) so the Watch can show 'near cap'. Do not change other caps.

Extend /api/admin/abuse (~line 11602) to also return the ai_source counts, last_fallback_reason, last_fallback_at, and a computed claude_pct_of_cap and near_cap boolean. Guarded by session founder_ok as today.

Surface it on The Watch dashboard (admin_dashboard ~line 13154, security/readout region ~line 14172 or the abuse panel): add a small, plain-language 'Live voice vs. built-in words' readout so the founder can SEE, today, how many replies came from the live AI vs. the built-in fallback and the reason for any fallback, plus a clear 'near daily limit' warning when near_cap. Plain words, no jargon, acronyms spelled out (AI = the live voice). Coordinate styling with existing Watch panels; do NOT introduce a new all-brown block — a calm readable accent is fine.

Add/extend the regression tool: in tools/ (alongside check_crisis_safety.py) add a small check that, with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset, /api/checkin still returns 200 with a warm reply (fallback path) and that the ai_source telemetry increments a fallback bucket — proving the hybrid degrades gracefully and is observable. Do NOT call the real API in the test.
acceptance_criteria: With no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set, /api/checkin returns 200 with a warm reply and the AI-source telemetry records a fallback with a reason (not a silent failure); the claude budget counter is NOT consumed when no key is present.
When the daily Claude cap is reached, a person in crisis is NOT turned away with a 'busy' 429 on /api/checkin; the request proceeds to the warm local fallback and telemetry marks fallback_budget.
The daily Claude budget counter is charged for actual Claude calls, not for every check-in message.
The API key is never printed or logged anywhere; grep confirms no code path logs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or its value.
GET /api/admin/abuse (as founder) returns ai_source counts, last_fallback_reason, and a near_cap indicator.
The Watch dashboard shows a plain-language live-voice-vs-built-in-words readout and a near-daily-limit warning.
Live Claude remains the PRIMARY path (hybrid preserved); the local lines are only fallback.
The full validation gate (py_compile, check_frontend 0 failures, lang parity, smoke) passes.
verification: cd /projects/sandbox/innerlight && python -m py_compile core/axiom_harmony_unified_app.py core/comprehension_engine.py && echo COMPILE_OK
grep -rniE 'print.*ANTHROPIC_API_KEY|log.*ANTHROPIC_API_KEY' core/ ; echo 'expect no key-logging matches'

env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY python - <<'PY'
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'core')
import axiom_harmony_unified_app as a
c=a.app.test_client()
r=c.post('/api/checkin', json={'message':'I feel hopeless and alone tonight'})
print('status', r.status_code)
j=r.get_json(); print('has response', bool(j.get('response')))
PY
findings: CONFIRMED THE ROOT CAUSE: _budget_ok('claude') was charged at the very top of /api/checkin on EVERY message (even with no key and even when Claude was never the decider), and when the cap (default 1500/day) was hit the whole crisis route returned _gentle_429() — a 'busy' turn-away, a dead end forbidden by Immutable Principle 1. So yes, the cap was starving real users onto the clinical/built-in fallback AND turning people away when exhausted. FIX: removed the top-of-route _budget_ok('claude') charge (kept the per-IP _rate_ok abuse limit + _gentle_429 for genuine rate abuse). Added _budget_room(kind) (checks room without consuming). The claude budget is now charged (via _budget_ok) ONLY immediately before an ACTUAL live call, and only when a key is present (comprehension_engine.available()) AND there is room; when no key is set, no claude budget is consumed. When the cap is reached, the request PROCEEDS to the warm built-in fallback and telemetry marks fallback_budget instead of a 429. Same pattern mirrored in /api/innerlight/learn (smart_l). TELEMETRY: added thread-safe _AI_SOURCE daily counter with _mark_ai_source(kind,reason) and buckets {live, fallback_no_key, fallback_api_error, fallback_over_line, fallback_budget, fallback_noneng, fallback_other} plus last_fallback_reason/last_fallback_at; every fallback logs a one-line reason via print (no key, no content). comprehension_engine now exposes last_fallback_reason() ('no_key'|'empty'|'api_error'|'over_line'|'') set inside respond()'s branches WITHOUT changing its dict-or-None return contract. Added _classify_ai_fallback() in the app to bucket by no-key/budget/language/engine reason. CONFIG: added CAP_CLAUDE_WARN_AT (default 80 percent) soft-warn threshold. WATCH: /api/admin/abuse (founder-guarded) now also returns ai_source counts, last_fallback_reason, last_fallback_at, claude_pct_of_cap, claude_warn_at, near_cap. Added a plain-language 'Live voice vs. built-in words' panel to The Watch (before the Security section) with a near-daily-limit warning, spelling out AI = the live voice, no jargon, using the existing gold accent (no new brown block). KEY SAFETY CONFIRMED: grep for 'print.*ANTHROPIC_API_KEY|log.*ANTHROPIC_API_KEY' in core/ returns nothing; telemetry stores only counts and short reason strings, never the key or any message/response content; the pre-existing str(e)[:120] print in respond() is unchanged. HYBRID PRESERVED: live Claude stays PRIMARY; built-in lines only fall back. Did NOT touch crisis fallback WORDING or the live SYSTEM_PROMPT (separate features). TESTS: added tools/check_hybrid_fallback.py (never calls the real API) proving no-key -> 200 warm reply + fallback_no_key + zero claude spend, and cap-reached -> 200 warm reply + fallback_budget (no 429); wired it into verify.sh. VERIFIED: py_compile OK (no SyntaxWarning) on both files; check_frontend now 38 script blocks / 0 failures (was 37; my new Watch panel block added); check_lang_parity exit 0 (bootstrap baseline unchanged); crisis-safety guard all green; hybrid guard all green; smoke test all green; full verify.sh exits VERIFIED. NOTE: flask/numpy/cryptography/gunicorn were not actually pre-installed in the 3.12.13 pyenv as the briefing stated — installed via 'pip install -r requirements.txt' (OPEN_INTERNET), the documented build command.
